---
title: "Norway's 2026 Household Liquidity Squeeze: Monetary Contraction, Childcare Costs, and Family Employment Patterns"
description: "How tightening money supply, rising childcare fees, and shifting employment across household types combine to reveal economic strain in Norwegian families."
date: "2026-09-04"
categories: [SSB, monetary-policy, households, childcare, employment]
---


Norwegian households are navigating a confluence of pressures rarely seen in combination: a contracting money supply, persistently high childcare costs, and diverging employment rates across family types. Together, these forces shape who can participate in the economy and how much liquidity remains in household budgets after essential expenses. This post draws on three Statistics Norway datasets to map the contours of that squeeze.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, error = TRUE)

library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(PxWebApiData)
library(scales)
library(MetBrewer)
library(ggridges)
library(stringr)

# --- Fetch df1: Money supply (table 10949) ---
df1 <- NULL
tryCatch({
  raw <- ApiData(
    "https://data.ssb.no/api/v0/no/table/10949",
    Eiersektor = TRUE,
    Pengemengden = TRUE,
    ContentsCode = TRUE,
    Tid = list(filter = "top", values = 40)
  )
  tmp          <- raw[[1]]
  time_col     <- "måned"
  value_col    <- "value"
  series_col   <- "pengemengden"
  measure_col  <- "statistikkvariabel"
  df1 <- tmp |>
    mutate(
      value    = as.numeric(.data[[value_col]]),
      time_str = .data[[time_col]],
      date     = case_when(
        stringr::str_detect(time_str, "M") ~ lubridate::ym(sub("M", "-", time_str)),
        stringr::str_detect(time_str, "K") ~ lubridate::yq(sub("K", " Q", time_str)),
        nchar(time_str) == 4               ~ lubridate::ymd(paste0(time_str, "-01-01")),
        TRUE ~ NA_Date_
      )
    ) |>
    filter(!is.na(value), !is.na(date))
}, error = function(e) message("Fetch failed: ", e$message))

if (is.null(df1) || nrow(df1) == 0) { message("No data returned for df1"); df1 <- NULL }

# --- Fetch df2: Employment by household type (table 14651) ---
df2 <- NULL
tryCatch({
  raw <- ApiData(

    Kjonn = TRUE,
    Alder = TRUE,
    HushType = TRUE,
    ContentsCode = TRUE,
    Tid = list(filter = "top", values = 40)
  )
  tmp          <- raw[[1]]
  time_col     <- "år"
  value_col    <- "value"
  series_col   <- "husholdningstype"
  measure_col  <- "statistikkvariabel"
  df2 <- tmp |>
    mutate(
      value    = as.numeric(.data[[value_col]]),
      time_str = .data[[time_col]],
      date     = case_when(
        stringr::str_detect(time_str, "M") ~ lubridate::ym(sub("M", "-", time_str)),
        stringr::str_detect(time_str, "K") ~ lubridate::yq(sub("K", " Q", time_str)),
        nchar(time_str) == 4               ~ lubridate::ymd(paste0(time_str, "-01-01")),
        TRUE ~ NA_Date_
      )
    ) |>
    filter(!is.na(value), !is.na(date))
}, error = function(e) message("Fetch failed: ", e$message))

if (is.null(df2) || nrow(df2) == 0) { message("No data returned for df2"); df2 <- NULL }

# --- Fetch df3: Childcare costs by municipality (table 11573) ---
df3 <- NULL
tryCatch({
  raw <- ApiData(
    "https://data.ssb.no/api/v0/no/table/11573",
    Region = TRUE,
    Tid = list(filter = "top", values = 40)

  time_col     <- "år"

        stringr::str_detect(time_str, "K") ~ lubridate::yq(sub("K", " Q", time_str)),
        nchar(time_str) == 4               ~ lubridate::ymd(paste0(time_str, "-01-01")),
```

## The Money Supply Signal: Reading M1, M2, and M3

Money supply aggregates are rarely front-page news in Norway, but their twelve-month growth rates carry a quiet signal about how much liquidity is circulating through the economy. When M1 — the most liquid aggregate, covering cash and overnight deposits — decelerates or contracts, households feel it first in their current accounts.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# --- df1 wrangling: money supply growth rates ---
df1_growth  <- NULL
df1_stocks  <- NULL

if (!is.null(df1) && nrow(df1) > 0) {
  # fixed: check actual column name and filter values
  df1_growth <- df1 |>
    filter(.data[["statistikkvariabel"]] == "Tolvmånedersvekst (prosent)") |>
    filter(.data[["pengetype"]] %in% c("M1", "M2", "M3"))
  if (nrow(df1_growth) == 0) {
    message("df1_growth empty. measure values: ",
            paste(head(unique(df1[["statistikkvariabel"]]), 10), collapse = ", "))
    df1_growth <- NULL
  }

  df1_stocks <- df1 |>
    filter(.data[["statistikkvariabel"]] == "Beholdninger (mill. kr)") |>
    filter(.data[["pengetype"]] %in% c("M1", "M2", "M3"))
  if (nrow(df1_stocks) == 0) {
    message("df1_stocks empty.")
    df1_stocks <- NULL
  }
}
```

## Who Is Working? Employment Across Household Structures

Employment rates differ sharply by family configuration. Single parents, lone-person households, and couples with children each face distinct barriers and incentives to work. Understanding these gaps matters because employment is the primary buffer against liquidity stress — a household without an earner is far more exposed to rising fixed costs.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
if (exists("df2_rate") && !is.null(df2_rate) && nrow(df2_rate) > 0) {

  # Shorten labels for readability
  df2_rate_plot <- df2_rate |>
    mutate(
      hush_label = case_when(
        .data[["husholdningstype"]] == "I alt"                                      ~ "All households",
        .data[["husholdningstype"]] == "Mor eller far med barn under 18"            ~ "Single parent",
        .data[["husholdningstype"]] == "Aleneboende"                                ~ "Living alone",
        .data[["husholdningstype"]] == "Person i parforhold med barn under 18 år"   ~ "Couple with children",
        .data[["husholdningstype"]] == "Person i parforhold uten barn under 18 år"  ~ "Couple without children",
        TRUE ~ .data[["husholdningstype"]]
      ),
      year = lubridate::year(date)
    ) |>
    filter(!is.na(value))

  pal_ridge <- MetBrewer::met.brewer("Hokusai2", n = length(unique(df2_rate_plot$hush_label)))

  p <- ggplot(df2_rate_plot,
              aes(x = value, y = hush_label, fill = hush_label, colour = hush_label)) +
    ggridges::geom_density_ridges(alpha = 0.55, bandwidth = 1.2,
                                   rel_min_height = 0.01, scale = 0.9) +
    scale_fill_manual(values  = pal_ridge, guide = "none") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = pal_ridge, guide = "none") +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
    labs(
      title    = "Distribution of employment rates by household type",
      subtitle = "Density of annual employment rate (%) across all available years — persons aged 15-74",
      x        = "Employment rate (%)",
      y        = NULL,
      caption  = "Source: Statistics Norway (SSB), table 14651"
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

  print(p) # fixed: added explicit print()

  latest_year  <- max(df2_rate_plot$year, na.rm = TRUE)
  latest_rates <- df2_rate_plot |>
    filter(year == latest_year) |>
    group_by(hush_label) |>
    summarise(mean_rate = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
    arrange(mean_rate)

  if (nrow(latest_rates) > 0) {
    lowest  <- latest_rates[1, ]
    highest <- latest_rates[nrow(latest_rates), ]
    cat(sprintf(
      "\nIn %d, '%s' recorded the lowest average employment rate (%.1f%%) while '%s' recorded the highest (%.1f%%).\n\n",
      latest_year, lowest$hush_label, lowest$mean_rate,
      highest$hush_label, highest$mean_rate
    ))
  }

} else {
  cat("\n*Figure omitted — Statistics Norway returned no data for this series.*\n\n")
}
```

## The Dumbbell View: Change in Employment Rates Over Time

Ridgeline charts capture the full distribution, but a dumbbell chart isolates directional change — showing which household types have seen employment rates rise or fall between the earliest and most recent years available.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
if (exists("df2_rate") && !is.null(df2_rate) && nrow(df2_rate) > 0) {

  df2_dumb <- df2_rate |>
    mutate(
      hush_label = case_when(
        .data[["husholdningstype"]] == "I alt"                                      ~ "All households",
        .data[["husholdningstype"]] == "Mor eller far med barn under 18"            ~ "Single parent",
        .data[["husholdningstype"]] == "Aleneboende"                                ~ "Living alone",
        .data[["husholdningstype"]] == "Person i parforhold med barn under 18 år"   ~ "Couple with children",
        .data[["husholdningstype"]] == "Person i parforhold uten barn under 18 år"  ~ "Couple without children",
        TRUE ~ .data[["husholdningstype"]]
      ),
      year = lubridate::year(date)
    ) |>
    group_by(hush_label, year) |>
    summarise(rate = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

  year_min <- min(df2_dumb$year, na.rm = TRUE)
  year_max <- max(df2_dumb$year, na.rm = TRUE)

  df2_dumb_wide <- df2_dumb |>
    filter(year %in% c(year_min, year_max)) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = rate,
                names_prefix = "yr_") |>
    rename(yr_start = paste0("yr_", year_min),
           yr_end   = paste0("yr_", year_max)) |>
    filter(!is.na(yr_start), !is.na(yr_end)) |>
    mutate(
      change    = yr_end - yr_start,
      direction = if_else(change >= 0, "Increase", "Decrease"),
      hush_label = fct_reorder(hush_label, yr_end)
    )

  if (nrow(df2_dumb_wide) == 0) {
    cat("\n*Figure omitted — insufficient data for dumbbell chart.*\n\n")
  } else {

    pal_db <- MetBrewer::met.brewer("Hokusai2", n = 2)

    p <- ggplot(df2_dumb_wide, aes(y = hush_label)) +
      geom_segment(aes(x = yr_start, xend = yr_end,
                       yend = hush_label, colour = direction),
                   linewidth = 1.2, lineend = "round") +
      geom_point(aes(x = yr_start), colour = pal_db[1], size = 4) +
      geom_point(aes(x = yr_end),   colour = pal_db[2], size = 4) +
      geom_text(aes(x = yr_end, label = sprintf("%.1f%%", yr_end)),
                hjust = -0.3, size = 3.2, colour = "grey30") +
      scale_colour_manual(values = c("Increase" = pal_db[2], "Decrease" = pal_db[1]),
                          name = "Direction") +
      scale_x_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"),
                         expand  = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.12))) +
      labs(
        title    = "Employment rate change by household type",
        subtitle = paste0("Comparison of average employment rates: ", year_min,
                          " (filled circle) vs ", year_max, " (open circle)"),
        x        = "Employment rate (%)",
        y        = NULL,
        caption  = "Source: Statistics Norway (SSB), table 14651"
      ) +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
      theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
            legend.position  = "top")

    print(p) # fixed: added explicit print()

    largest_gain <- df2_dumb_wide |> slice_max(change, n = 1)
    largest_drop <- df2_dumb_wide |> slice_min(change, n = 1)

    cat(sprintf(
      "\nBetween %d and %d, '%s' saw the largest gain in employment rate (+%.1f percentage points) while '%s' saw the largest decline (%.1f pp).\n\n",
      year_min, year_max,
      largest_gain$hush_label[1], largest_gain$change[1],
      largest_drop$hush_label[1], largest_drop$change[1]
    ))
  }

} else {
  cat("\n*Figure omitted — Statistics Norway returned no data for this series.*\n\n")
}
```

## Childcare Costs: A Municipal Lens

Childcare fees represent one of the most direct fixed costs for families with young children. Even with national fee caps, actual prices can vary across municipalities, and the trend over time reveals how quickly this burden has grown relative to wages. The municipalities captured here — covering the Østfold region and the national average — provide a concrete geographic anchor for the analysis.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
if (exists("df3_monthly") && !is.null(df3_monthly) && nrow(df3_monthly) > 0) {

  df3_plot <- df3_monthly |>
    mutate(
      year      = lubridate::year(date),
      region_lbl = .data[["region"]]
    )

  latest_yr   <- max(df3_plot$year, na.rm = TRUE)
  df3_latest  <- df3_plot |>
    filter(year == latest_yr) |>
    group_by(region_lbl) |>
    summarise(avg_cost = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
    arrange(avg_cost) |>
    mutate(region_lbl = fct_inorder(region_lbl))

  if (nrow(df3_latest) == 0) {
    cat("\n*Figure omitted — no data for latest year in childcare series.*\n\n")
  } else {

    pal_lol <- MetBrewer::met.brewer("Hokusai2", n = 1)

    p <- ggplot(df3_latest, aes(x = avg_cost, y = region_lbl)) +
      geom_segment(aes(x = 0, xend = avg_cost, yend = region_lbl),
                   colour = "grey75", linewidth = 0.8) +
      geom_point(colour = pal_lol, size = 5) +
      geom_text(aes(label = scales::comma(avg_cost, accuracy = 1, big.mark = " ")),
                hjust = -0.35, size = 3.3, colour = "grey25") +
      scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::comma_format(big.mark = " "),
                         expand  = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.18))) +
      labs(
        title    = paste0("Average monthly childcare price by municipality, ", latest_yr),
        subtitle = "Mean monthly barnehage price including free places — selected Østfold municipalities and national average",
        x        = "NOK per month",
        y        = NULL,
        caption  = "Source: Statistics Norway (SSB), table 11573"
      ) +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
      theme(panel.grid.minor  = element_blank(),
            panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())

    print(p) # fixed: added explicit print()

    top_muni    <- df3_latest |> slice_max(avg_cost, n = 1)
    bottom_muni <- df3_latest |> slice_min(avg_cost, n = 1)
    spread      <- top_muni$avg_cost[1] - bottom_muni$avg_cost[1]

    cat(sprintf(
      "\nIn %d, %s had the highest average monthly childcare cost (NOK %s) while %s had the lowest (NOK %s) — a spread of NOK %s.\n\n",
      latest_yr,
      top_muni$region_lbl[1],    scales::comma(top_muni$avg_cost[1],    big.mark = " "),
      bottom_muni$region_lbl[1], scales::comma(bottom_muni$avg_cost[1], big.mark = " "),
      scales::comma(spread, big.mark = " ")
    ))
  }

} else {
  cat("\n*Figure omitted — Statistics Norway returned no data for this series.*\n\n")
}
```

## Childcare Cost Trajectories Over Time

A single-year snapshot of childcare fees tells only part of the story. Tracking the trajectory across multiple years — as a small-multiples chart by municipality — reveals whether the gap between regions is widening, narrowing, or stable, and at what rate families are absorbing rising costs.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
if (exists("df3_monthly") && !is.null(df3_monthly) && nrow(df3_monthly) > 0) {

  df3_trend <- df3_monthly |>
    mutate(year = lubridate::year(date)) |>
    group_by(region_lbl = .data[["region"]], year) |>
    summarise(avg_cost = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

  if (nrow(df3_trend) == 0) {
    cat("\n*Figure omitted — no trend data for childcare series.*\n\n")
  } else {

    pal_sm <- MetBrewer::met.brewer("Hokusai2", n = 3)

    p <- ggplot(df3_trend, aes(x = year, y = avg_cost)) +
      geom_area(fill = pal_sm[1], alpha = 0.25) +
      geom_line(colour = pal_sm[2], linewidth = 1.0) +
      geom_point(colour = pal_sm[3], size = 1.8) +
      facet_wrap(~ region_lbl, scales = "free_y") +
      scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma_format(big.mark = " ")) +
      scale_x_continuous(breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 4)) +
      labs(
        title    = "Monthly childcare cost trend by municipality",
        subtitle = "Average monthly barnehage price (NOK) including free places — annual series per municipality",
        x        = NULL,
        y        = "NOK per month",
        caption  = "Source: Statistics Norway (SSB), table 11573"
      ) +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
      theme(
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        strip.text       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9),
        axis.text.x      = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1)
      )

    print(p) # fixed: added explicit print()

    first_yr     <- min(df3_trend$year, na.rm = TRUE)
    last_yr      <- max(df3_trend$year, na.rm = TRUE)
    growth_tbl   <- df3_trend |>
      filter(year %in% c(first_yr, last_yr)) |>
      pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = avg_cost,
                  names_prefix = "yr_") |>
      rename(yr_start = paste0("yr_", first_yr),
             yr_end   = paste0("yr_", last_yr)) |>
      filter(!is.na(yr_start), !is.na(yr_end)) |>
      mutate(pct_change = (yr_end - yr_start) / yr_start * 100) |>
      arrange(desc(pct_change))

    if (nrow(growth_tbl) > 0) {
      top_grower <- growth_tbl[1, ]
      cat(sprintf(
        "\nBetween %d and %d, %s recorded the steepest cumulative increase in monthly childcare costs (+%.1f%%).\n\n",
        first_yr, last_yr,
        top_grower$region_lbl[1],
        top_grower$pct_change[1]
      ))
    }
  }

} else {
  cat("\n*Figure omitted — Statistics Norway returned no data for this series.*\n\n")
}
```

## Closing Reflection

The three threads examined here — monetary contraction, household employment patterns, and childcare costs — are rarely analyzed together, yet they converge on the same pressure point: the cash flow available to Norwegian families after essential fixed costs are met. A tighter money supply reduces the buffer; lower employment rates in vulnerable household types reduce the income; and rising childcare fees increase the outgoings. The squeeze does not affect all households equally. Lone parents and single-person households occupy structurally different positions than dual-income couples, and the regional variation in childcare costs adds a geographic dimension to what is often discussed as a uniform national phenomenon. As monetary policy continues to work through the system and fee structures are renegotiated, these data offer a grounded baseline for tracking who absorbs the adjustment — and who does not.
